meta.name: Manage client onboarding and project handoff with Google Sheets and Gmail

name: Automate Client Onboarding And Project Handoff With Google Sheets And Gmail

parameters.content:
## Automate Client Onboarding And Project Handoff With Google Sheets And Gmail

### How it works

This workflow automates client onboarding from a webhook intake, validates and enriches the submission with Google Sheets data, then creates CRM, project handoff, and checklist records. It sends client and internal handoff emails, branches for duplicates or PM-attention cases, and returns an appropriate webhook response. A separate scheduled path runs every morning to identify active onboarding risks and email a digest when needed.

### Setup steps

- Configure the webhook endpoint used by the client intake form or system, and ensure it receives all fields expected by the validation and planning code nodes.
- Connect Google Sheets credentials and select the spreadsheets/tabs for existing clients, onboarding configuration, CRM rows, project handoff rows, onboarding checklists, active projects, and risk logs.
- Connect Gmail credentials for duplicate review, client welcome, internal handoff, PM alert, and risk digest emails.
- Review the code nodes to confirm required field names, duplicate matching rules, onboarding plan logic, and risk digest criteria match your sheet schema.
- Set the morning schedule trigger to the desired timezone and run time.

### Customization

You can adjust duplicate detection, onboarding checklist templates, PM-attention rules, risk scoring, email recipients, and email copy in the code, IF, Google Sheets, and Gmail nodes.

## Client onboarding and project handoff automation

This workflow turns a signed client into a structured onboarding record, project handoff, checklist, welcome email, and internal team alert. It is designed for small agencies that close leads manually but need a repeatable handoff process before delivery work begins.

### How it works

1. A website form, CRM, payment tool, or custom API sends new client data to the webhook.
2. The workflow validates required fields, normalizes service details, creates stable IDs, and calculates onboarding dates.
3. Google Sheets is used as a lightweight CRM and project operations tracker.
4. Duplicate clients are routed to review before another onboarding is created.
5. Approved clients receive a welcome email while the delivery team receives a handoff summary.
6. Rush, high-value, missing-date, or VIP-service clients are logged and escalated.
7. A scheduled branch sends a daily digest for stalled or risky onboarding records.

### Customization

Adjust onboarding stages, kickoff windows, risk thresholds, email copy, and config values to match your agency process.

## 1. Receive and validate client data

The webhook accepts signed client details from a form, CRM, checkout page, or custom API.

The Code node checks required fields, normalizes email and service names, creates a client ID and project ID, and prepares the record for repeatable onboarding.

## 2. Check existing clients and settings

The workflow reads the `Clients` tab to detect duplicate active clients.

It also reads the `Onboarding Config` tab so owners, kickoff timing, and VIP service rules can be changed without editing workflow logic.

## 4. Create CRM, project, and checklist records

New clients are appended to `Clients`, `Projects`, and `Onboarding Checklist`.

These rows create a simple operating system for the agency, so onboarding does not depend on memory or scattered emails.

## 5. Send handoff emails and escalate risk

Sends the client welcome and internal handoff emails, then evaluates whether the onboarding requires PM attention.

## 6. Daily onboarding risk digest

A scheduled branch reviews active onboarding records every morning.

It alerts the team when kickoff dates are overdue, checklist progress is blocked, or a client has been sitting in onboarding too long.

## Google Sheets setup

`Clients`: Created At | Client ID | Client Name | Client Email | Company | Service | Package | Budget | Project Manager | Priority | Status | Missing Info | Notes

`Projects`: Created At | Project ID | Client ID | Client Name | Service | Package | Start Date | Kickoff Target | Owner | Priority | Current Stage | Risk Level | Handoff Summary

`Onboarding Checklist`: Created At | Project ID | Client ID | Client Name | Checklist Items | Owner | Due Date | Status

`Onboarding Config`: Key | Value

`Onboarding Risk Log`: Logged At | Project ID | Client ID | Client Name | Risk Level | Reason | Owner | Recommended Action | Status

parameters.content:
## Send risk digest

Checks whether the daily digest contains onboarding risks and sends the digest email when risks are present.

## 3. Handle duplicate client

Sends an email for duplicate review and responds to the webhook indicating that an existing client match was found.

## 3. Plan and check duplicate

The plan node combines the client request, CRM history, and config values.

It calculates kickoff target date, priority, checklist items, missing information, and whether the client needs special project manager attention.

## Return standard success

Sends the normal webhook response when onboarding was created and no PM attention branch is needed.

## Escalate PM attention

For higher-risk onboarding cases, logs the risk, sends a PM alert email, and responds to the webhook that the onboarding was created with attention required.
